h1:
Diving in Thailand
Where to Learn & Where to Dive
intro: Thailand is one of the most accessible and affordable places in the world to learn and explore diving. The water is warm year-round, and there are sites for complete beginners as well as deep, world-class dives. The key is picking the right coast for your travel dates — the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea peak at opposite times of year. This guide covers where to learn, what each sea offers, seasons, and approximate course prices.
chips: 🏝️ Koh Tao = best value to learn
quickAnswerHtml: To learn to dive affordably, Koh Tao is the go-to — Open Water course 3–4 days for around 9,000–11,000 THB, tons of dive schools, shallow bays with calm water, and ideal conditions for beginners. For world-class dive sites, head to the Similan Islands (Andaman), which are only open mid-Oct to mid-May. Seasonal rule: Andaman coast (Similan, Phuket, Phi Phi, Koh Lipe) is best Nov–Apr; the Gulf coast (Koh Tao, Samui, Phangan) is diveable almost year-round — avoid heavy rains Oct–Dec. First-timers who aren't ready for a certification course can start with Discover Scuba (guided intro dive, no card required).

blocks.html: What makes Thailand such a great diving destination is warm water year-round, lower course costs compared with most countries, and a huge variety of sites — from shallow beginner bays to deep rock pinnacles where whale sharks pass through seasonally. The only planning decision is choosing the right coast for the month you're visiting.

blocks.html: The key to planning is which coast you're on. The Andaman coast (Phuket, Phi Phi, Similan, Koh Lipe) has clear water and calm conditions Nov–Apr. The Similan Islands, a national park, are only open roughly mid-October to mid-May, then close for the monsoon season to allow natural recovery. The Gulf coast (Koh Tao, Samui, Phangan) is diveable almost year-round; the period to avoid is heavy rainfall Oct–Dec. So if you arrive on the Andaman coast during monsoon season, you can switch to the Gulf side instead.

blocks.title: Dive Safely and Get the Most Value

items.title: Match the coast to the season
items.text: If you're on the Andaman coast during monsoon (May–Oct), switch to the Gulf side instead. For Similan, you must come during the open season: Oct–May.

items.title: Wait before flying
items.text: After deep dives, wait at least 18–24 hours before boarding a flight. Schedule your dive days so they don't clash with your departure day.

items.title: Compare dive school standards
items.text: Check whether the school is a PADI or SSI center, read reviews, and ask about the instructor-to-student ratio before booking.

items.title: Dive responsibly
items.text: Don't touch or stand on coral, don't feed fish, and use reef-safe sunscreen.

faq.q: Where is the best place to learn to dive in Thailand?
faq.a: Koh Tao is the most popular choice for learning — it has the most dive schools, shallow bays with calm conditions that suit beginners, and Open Water courses that are among the most affordable in the world.

faq.q: How long does an Open Water course take and what does it cost?
faq.a: Typically 3–4 days. On Koh Tao, prices run around 9,000–11,000 THB, covering theory, pool sessions, and open-water dives. Exact prices depend on the school and time of year — check when booking.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive in Thailand?
faq.a: The Andaman coast (Phuket, Phi Phi, Similan, Koh Lipe) is best Nov–Apr. The Similan Islands national park is only open roughly mid-Oct to mid-May. The Gulf coast (Koh Tao, Samui, Phangan) is diveable almost year-round — avoid heavy rainfall Oct–Dec.

faq.q: Can I dive without a certification card?
faq.a: Yes. Beginners can start with Discover Scuba — a guided intro dive with an instructor by your side, no card required. You can also choose snorkeling, which needs no training at all; day trips are available at every island.

faq.q: When are the Similan Islands closed?
faq.a: The Similan Islands are a national park, open only from roughly mid-October to mid-May. They close during the monsoon season to allow the ecosystem to recover, so plan your visit strictly within the open window.
